candidate.answerReason: The boundary consists of four outward semicircles surrounding a diamond of area 2, together with an isolated origin. Each semicircle has area pi/4, giving total area pi+2.

methods.label: Identify the circular arcs in each quadrant
methods.explanation:
Changing the sign of either coordinate leaves the equation unchanged, so the enclosed region has four congruent quadrant portions. It is enough to understand the first quadrant.

For \(x,y\ge0\), the equation becomes \(x^2+y^2=x+y\). Completing the squares gives
\[
\left(x-\frac12\right)^2+
\left(y-\frac12\right)^2=\frac12.
\]
This is a circle with center \((1/2,1/2)\) and radius squared \(1/2\). Let \(P=(1,0)\) and \(Q=(0,1)\). Their midpoint is the center, so \(PQ\) is a diameter. The semicircle on the side \(x+y\ge1\) lies in the first quadrant.

We must also check whether the other half of this circle contributes any further arcs there. Set \(s=x+y\). If \(0<s<1\), then, because \(x,y\ge0\),
\[
x^2+y^2\le(x+y)^2=s^2<s,
\]
so the original equation cannot hold. If \(s=0\), the only point is the origin \(O\); if \(s=1\), the equation gives only \(P\) and \(Q\). Thus the first-quadrant graph consists of the outward semicircle and the isolated origin.

The enclosed first-quadrant portion is triangle \(OPQ\), with area \(1/2\), together with the semidisk beyond \(PQ\), with area
\[
\frac12\pi r^2=\frac12\pi\left(\frac12\right)=\frac\pi4.
\]
The four portions have disjoint interiors. The isolated origin adds no area and creates no additional enclosed region. Therefore the total area is
\[
4\left(\frac12+\frac\pi4\right)
=\boxed{\pi+2},
\]
choice \(\boxed{B}\).
